## Objective
- Rework the existing game into a playable RTS inspired by Command & Conquer: Generals, with faction selection, faction-specific forces, open-map resource harvesting, construction, and progression.

## Requirements
- Support USA, China, and Russia, each with distinct buildings and troops.
- Open map where players harvest resources to build structures, defenses, and units.
- Building types should unlock further buildings, defenses, and troops.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Added faction-specific stat bonuses and names, plus faction-themed visual details.
- Added a tech-center progression step and production queues; units are no longer spawned instantly.
- Expanded the map’s resource nodes and adjusted enemy attack timing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing game and its HTML, JavaScript, 3D renderer, styles, and README.
- Updated faction identities, unit bonuses, construction prerequisites, production queues, resource node count, and enemy timing in `game.js`.
- Added tech-center building visuals and faction-specific model details in `renderer3d.js`.
- Added a faction doctrine display and changed starting field-force count in `index.html`.

### Active
- Validate the game in-browser and fix any gameplay or rendering issues.
- Review progression and faction differences against the requested Generals-style gameplay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current changes in `game.js`, `renderer3d.js`, and `index.html` for runtime or logic errors.
2. Run the game and test faction selection, harvesting, building placement, prerequisites, unit production, and victory/defeat.
3. Capture and inspect the latest gameplay screenshot; refine UI or gameplay as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: RTS simulation, faction data, economy, progression, and controls.
- `renderer3d.js`: Three.js battlefield and faction/building/unit models.
- `index.html`: Game UI, faction selection, briefing, command options.
- `styles.css`: Game layout and responsive styles.
- `start.sh`: Game launch script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests, browser validation, or screenshots have been run yet.
- `tech` was added to `buildingStats` and the build menu; tanks require both factory and tech center.
- The faction doctrine display currently uses an inline `<style>` block in `index.html`.

- Provide an open map for harvesting resources and building structures, defenses, and units.
- Building types should unlock further buildings, defenses, and troops.
- Make reasonable assumptions; do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Added faction-specific names, doctrines, stat bonuses, and visual details.
- Added tech-center progression, queued unit production, more resource nodes, and delayed enemy attacks.
- Attack orders retain an explicit target while units move into range; direct movement clears prior attack targets.
- Unit movement is restricted to units, preventing buildings from moving to invalid coordinates during simulation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated faction data, bonuses, construction prerequisites, production queues, resource node count, enemy timing, and interaction behavior.
- Added tech-center and faction-specific model details; updated doctrine display and starting field-force count.
- Fixed build faction reference, faction-specific prerequisite toasts, doctrine synchronization, attack/movement behavior, and buildings being processed by the unit movement loop.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser verified China construction progression, infantry production completion, and harvesting income; USA and Russia faction selection and deployment display correct labels, doctrines, starting credits, and units.

- Finish browser verification of combat, victory/defeat, and faction-specific construction for USA and Russia.
- Review changed files and rerun checks after any further changes.

- (none)

2. Verify USA and Russia construction in the real browser; the latest Russia construction attempt was inconclusive.
3. Review changes and rerun `node --check game.js`, `node --check renderer3d.js`, and `git diff --check`.

- `game.js`: RTS simulation, faction data, economy, progression, controls, movement, and combat.
- `renderer3d.js`: Three.js battlefield and faction/building/unit models.
- `index.html`: Game UI, faction selection, briefing, and command options.
- `styles.css`: Game layout and responsive styles.
- `/tmp/opencode/rts-started.png`: Browser screenshot after deployment.

- Browser console previously reported a 404 for `/favicon.ico`; no other application errors were observed.

## Objective
- Rework the existing game into a playable RTS inspired by Command & Conquer: Generals, with faction choice, distinct forces, resource harvesting, construction, and progression.
- Make the game mobile-friendly, with easier map navigation and unit selection, and improve map, unit, and building graphics.

## Requirements
- Support USA, China, and Russia with distinct buildings and troops.
- Provide an open map for harvesting resources and building structures, defenses, and units; buildings unlock further options.
- Ensure phone players can scroll the map and easily select units and soldiers.
- Improve visual detail beyond the current blocky graphics.
- Make reasonable assumptions; do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Added faction-specific names, doctrines, stat bonuses, and visual details.
- Added tech-center progression, queued unit production, more resource nodes, and delayed enemy attacks.
- Attack orders retain an explicit target while units move into range; direct movement clears prior attack targets.
- Unit movement is restricted to units, preventing buildings from moving during simulation.
- Began mobile input work with gesture-state variables and a slightly closer initial zoom.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented faction progression, construction prerequisites, production queues, harvesting, combat behavior, and faction-specific models.
- Verified China construction progression, infantry production, and harvesting in a browser; USA and Russia selection/deployment labels, doctrines, credits, and starting units appeared correctly.
- Added `mapGesture`, `touchPoints`, and `pinch` state to `game.js` and set initial camera zoom to `1.12`.

### Active
- Implement mobile-friendly map panning/zooming and improve touch selection; gesture state is declared but not yet wired to events.
- Improve battlefield, unit, and building visual detail.
- Complete browser verification of combat, victory/defeat, and faction-specific construction for USA and Russia.
- Review changes and rerun checks after changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement touch drag panning and pinch zoom on the battlefield, while preserving tap-to-select and tap-to-command interactions.
2. Improve map and model detail while considering mobile rendering performance.
3. Verify mobile behavior and finish browser testing for combat, victory/defeat, and USA/Russia construction.
4. Run `node --check game.js`, `node --check renderer3d.js`, and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: RTS simulation, map input, economy, progression, controls, movement, and combat.
- `renderer3d.js`: Three.js battlefield, terrain, and faction/building/unit models.
- `styles.css`: Game layout and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Game UI, faction selection, briefing, and command options.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `renderer3d.js`, and `index.html`; additional mobile-related state was just added to `game.js`.
- Browser is available at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/` via Chromium remote debugging on port `9222`.
- `/tmp/opencode/rts-started.png` is a prior browser screenshot.
- Browser console previously reported a 404 for `/favicon.ico`; no other application errors were observed.

## Objective
- Rework the existing game into a playable RTS inspired by Command & Conquer: Generals, with faction choice, distinct forces, resource harvesting, construction, and progression.
- Improve mobile playability and visual detail.

## Requirements
- Support USA, China, and Russia with distinct buildings and troops.
- Provide an open map for harvesting resources and building structures, defenses, and units; buildings unlock further options.
- Make map navigation and unit selection easy on phones.
- Improve map, unit, and building graphics beyond blocky visuals.
- Make reasonable assumptions; do not ask clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Added faction-specific names, doctrines, stat bonuses, and visual details.
- Added tech-center progression, queued unit production, more resource nodes, and delayed enemy attacks.
- Attack orders retain an explicit target while units move into range; direct movement clears prior attack targets.
- Unit movement is restricted to units, preventing buildings from moving during simulation.
- Initial camera zoom is `1.12`; zoom is bounded between `0.8` and `1.8`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented faction progression, construction prerequisites, production queues, harvesting, combat behavior, and faction-specific models.
- Verified China construction progression, infantry production, and harvesting in a browser; USA and Russia selection/deployment labels, doctrines, credits, and starting units appeared correctly.
- Added pointer-based map dragging, pinch-to-zoom, cursor-anchored wheel zoom, camera clamping, and larger touch selection radius.
- Updated on-screen navigation hint to “DRAG TO PAN · PINCH TO ZOOM”.
- `node --check game.js`, `node --check renderer3d.js`, and `git diff --check` passed after the input changes.

### Active
- Verify touch gestures, combat, victory/defeat, and USA/Russia construction in the browser.
- Review battlefield/model detail and mobile rendering behavior.
- Re-run checks after any further changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test touch drag, pinch zoom, taps, and touch selection in browser, confirming taps still issue orders.
2. Verify combat, victory/defeat, and USA/Russia construction progression.
3. Review mobile rendering and visuals; make any needed fixes.
4. Run `node --check game.js`, `node --check renderer3d.js`, and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: RTS simulation, map input, economy, progression, controls, movement, and combat.
- `renderer3d.js`: Three.js battlefield, terrain, and faction/building/unit models.
- `styles.css`: Game layout and responsive styles.
- `index.html`: Game UI, faction selection, briefing, and mobile navigation hint.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `renderer3d.js`, and `index.html`.
- Browser is available at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/` via Chromium remote debugging on port `9222`; prior console only reported a 404 for `/favicon.ico`.
